title: Large Deviation Principle for the Empirical Measures of Simple Random Walks on $\overline{\mathbb{Z}}$
summary: In this article we establish a large deviation principle for the empirical measures of a simple spatially inhomogeneous random walk on $\overline{\mathbb{Z}}$, the two-point compactification of $\mathbb{Z}$. The classical Donsker--Varadhan framework does not apply, since the random-walk kernel and the topology of $\overline{\mathbb{Z}}$ fall outside its standard assumptions. In certain regimes, the resulting rate function is non-convex on its effective domain.
